title.rendered: Apple’s new ‘genai.apple.com’ subdomain hints at bigger AI plans ahead of WWDC 2026

content.rendered:
Apple appears to be preparing a new web destination focused on AI, as a newly discovered subdomain points to possible announcements ahead of WWDC 2026.

According to Aaron Perris from MacRumors, Apple has added genai.apple.com to its domain records, although the page is not live yet.

A new AI subdomain appears ahead of WWDC

The “genai” naming strongly suggests a focus on generative AI, an area that has rapidly grown in popularity through tools like ChatGPT and Claude.

Apple already has a dedicated Apple Intelligence page on its website, so the purpose of this new subdomain remains unclear. It could serve as a central hub for Apple’s broader AI efforts or highlight new features expected to be announced at WWDC.

The timing is notable, as Apple has already confirmed that this year’s developer conference will include major AI-related updates across its platforms.

iOS 27 and Siri upgrades could be at the center of Apple’s AI push

Apple’s upcoming software updates, including iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27, are expected to introduce several new Apple Intelligence features.

Reports suggest Apple is working on a more personalized version of Siri with on-screen awareness, allowing it to understand what users are looking at and respond accordingly.

A more advanced Siri experience may also include a dedicated interface for back-and-forth conversations, similar to modern AI chatbots.

Apple Intelligence is also expected to power new features such as:

  • Automatic captions for personal videos
  • More natural language control in Voice Control
  • Easier shortcut creation in the Shortcuts app
  • A new “Create a Pass” option in Wallet
  • Smarter tab grouping in Safari
  • Visual Intelligence tools for scanning labels and documents

Apple’s WWDC 2026 keynote kicks off on June 8, where the company is expected to share more details about its AI roadmap.

Do you think Apple needs a separate AI platform like genai.apple.com, or should everything stay under Apple Intelligence? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to use Gemini for WhatsApp messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says Gemini interactions depend on the permissions and connected app settings you allow. You can disable WhatsApp integration anytime inside Gemini settings. Personally, I would avoid using it when discussing banking matters or any personal stuff, such as passwords and work details.

mainEntity.name: Can Gemini reply automatically?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. Gemini assists you in composing replies and sending them using voice commands. But it does not autonomously run your WhatsApp conversations. You’re still the one approving and sending messages.

title.rendered: How to avoid getting hacked on Roblox

content.rendered:
Those who play live-service games like Roblox are often a prime target of hackers and scammers. That’s because the presence of microtransactions in such games ensures that bad actors have a chance to orchestrate elaborate shams to trick users into sharing their account’s sensitive details by falsely offering in-game currency.

Similar incidents in the past have resulted in Roblox players losing access to their accounts. While sometimes these scammers use free Robux as bait, other instances have seen players get locked out of their accounts simply for following poor account security practices. The following tips will help you navigate any potential risks and upgrade the security of your Roblox account.

Tips to protect your Roblox account from hackers

1. Add your email to Roblox

If you haven’t yet, I strongly suggest you take the easiest first step towards securing your Roblox account by linking your personal email ID. Ensure the ID you give is your primary one because the game will use it for crucial account security and account recovery actions, such as 2-step verification setup and password reset, respectively.

Here are the steps to connect your email with your Roblox account:

  1. Go to roblox.com, log in to your account and click on the gear icon at the top-right corner.
  2. Alternatively, if you’re using the Roblox app, log in and click on “More” (three-dots button) near the left edge of the screen.
  3. From the menu that appears, select ‘Settings’.
  4. In the ‘Account Info’ tab, look for the ‘Email Address‘ section and click on ‘Add‘. If your account has an existing linked email, an edit button will show instead, using which you can link a different email ID in case you want to.
  5. Check your email inbox for Roblox’s verification mail and follow the instructions mentioned therein.

2. Only click on official Roblox links

Speaking of emails, you may receive some from Roblox occasionally, depending on your notification settings. However, there may also be spam emails containing malicious links disguised as Roblox. To tell these two apart, check the email and verify the sender’s address ends in “@roblox.com.”

To verify the authenticity of the links and clickable parts in such emails, repeat the same process and check that the website domain starts with “https://www.roblox.com/”. In some cases, the website destination of those clickable parts in the email may only appear near the bottom edge of the screen when you hover the mouse cursor over it.

3. Enable 2SV for better security

In this day and age, 2-Step Verification (2SV) is increasingly becoming a must for safeguarding your online accounts, be it Roblox or anything else. This security measure involves two steps to verify ownership of an account before any major changes, such as a change of linked email, can happen. In Roblox’s case, you can either use your email or an authenticator app or a combination of both for 2SV.

For enabling 2SV, a verified linked email is a prerequisite. Once that’s taken care of, you may follow the steps below.

  1. Open your Roblox, click on the gear icon or the “More” button and select “Settings.”
  2. Select the “Security” section and choose your desired option for 2SV. In this example, we will choose email.
  3. After you click on your preferred 2SV method, a pop-up will appear in which you have to enter the code sent to your linked email. Once entered, click on “Verify” to complete the setup.
  4. Post this, you will also receive a confirmation email in your inbox.

4. Don’t fall for Robux scams

As is common with most games that have some sort of in-game currency or microtransactions involved, you will possibly stumble upon offers of free Robux in exchange for personal details. But it’s worth remembering that Roblox doesn’t allow third-party vendors to provide Robux on its behalf. So, in virtually all cases, ads promoting free Robux are scams that often steal your personal information via surveys and forms.

There are only very few exceptions to this rule—one being Microsoft Rewards, which in certain regions, gives players 100 Robux for free. Another official way to get free Robux is by paying for certain Roblox Plus subscription bundles, which credit up to 2000 Robux to your balance every month. However, these bundles have only recently been announced in April and are not out yet.

5. Beware of shady games within Roblox

It is important to keep in mind that your username and password is only required on the Roblox website or its app and nowhere else. You should strictly avoid entering the same in any kind of other webpage or form even if it appears to closely resemble the official site.

Roblox itself warns players that, in the off-chance that a game or experience within the platform asks to submit passwords, they should not proceed further and should flag that particular Roblox experience using the “Report Abuse” option under the description (as shown in the image below).

6. Be careful with browser extensions made for Roblox

Although Roblox doesn’t have an official browser extension, there are several from third parties that provide certain quality-of-life features for players, such as custom themes and an FPS counter. I, too, admit these community creations can be useful at times. But in some cases, hackers may also use these extensions to carry on malicious practices.

For that reason, always make sure that you download Roblox-oriented browser extensions from legitimate stores, such as the Google Chrome Store and Safari Extensions. Even then, you’d be safer sticking to only those extensions that are rated highly and have received a large number of reviews. I’d reckon not considering extensions rated below 4 out of 5 and having fewer than a thousand user review scores. For that, you may use store filters to show only those results that meet your criteria.

Wrapping up

The aforementioned guidelines are the least that you can do to consolidate your Roblox account’s security. Apart from these tips, it goes without saying that you must also follow other obvious rules for safe internet usage, such as avoiding suspicious downloads and websites with expired security certificates.

In case you detect anything suspicious with your account, reporting it to Roblox’s support team, via the official website form, should be a priority. Prompt reporting is especially crucial when account access is at risk, in order to maximize the chances of successful recovery.

Must read: All Roblox Icons and Symbols Mean…

FAQs

Which Roblox account details are sensitive information?

Details such as your password and two-step verification code are sensitive information and should never be shared with others.

What happens if my Roblox account gets hacked?

If your Roblox account falls victim to a hack, firstly, you may lose all access to it. That means losing your in-game progress in Roblox experiences, your Robux balance, your inventory items such as Limiteds, and even saved payment details. Importantly, you should inform Roblox’s support team in the event that you lose account access.

Can I share my email linked to Roblox with others?

Yes, it is generally safe to share your email linked to Roblox with others. However, you should never share other critical Roblox account details, like your password, with anyone else.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to use Gemini for WhatsApp messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says Gemini interactions depend on the permissions and connected app settings you allow. You can disable WhatsApp integration anytime inside Gemini settings. Personally, I would avoid using it when discussing banking matters or any personal stuff, such as passwords and work details.

mainEntity.name: Can Gemini reply automatically?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. Gemini assists you in composing replies and sending them using voice commands. But it does not autonomously run your WhatsApp conversations. You’re still the one approving and sending messages.

mainEntity.name: Which Roblox account details are sensitive information?

acceptedAnswer.text: Details such as your password and two-step verification code are sensitive information and should never be shared with others.

mainEntity.name: What happens if my Roblox account gets hacked?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your Roblox account falls victim to a hack, firstly, you may lose all access to it. That means losing your in-game progress in Roblox experiences, your Robux balance, your inventory items such as Limiteds, and even saved payment details. Importantly, you should inform Roblox's support team in the event that you lose account access.

mainEntity.name: Can I share my email linked to Roblox with others?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it is generally safe to share your email linked to Roblox with others. However, you should never share other critical Roblox account details, like your password, with anyone else.

title.rendered: Apple Wallet can now track more than just Apple Pay orders in iOS 26

content.rendered:
Order tracking is not new to the Wallet app, but that experience was limited. It worked nicely with the orders from participating merchants paid through Apple Pay. But whenever I made purchases from anywhere else, I was back digging through Mail, copying tracking numbers, and opening courier sites to view the shipment status.

iOS 26 finally fixes the most annoying part. The Wallet app now shows shipment details in one place, thanks to Apple Intelligence in Mail. In this guide, I’ll show you how to turn on order tracking in iOS 26 Wallet, where to find your orders, and what to do if your shipments are not showing up.

What is order tracking in the iOS 26 Wallet app? 

Order Tracking in the Wallet app is Apple’s built-in way to keep your online purchase updates in one place. This feature has already existed since iOS 16 for eligible Apple Pay purchases from participating merchants. But it felt half-finished as most sellers had their own tracking system and didn’t bother to tie up with Apple.

However, in iOS 26, Wallet can now also use Apple Intelligence to find supported order information from your emails sent from sellers, marketplaces, and courier companies. So even if an order was not added through Apple Pay, it may still appear in Wallet. No need to manually paste tracking numbers.

Note that this does not mean Wallet will track every single shipment automatically. It works with eligible purchases, supported merchants, and order emails that Wallet can understand. You will see a Found in Mail label to distinguish them.

Apple Pay orders vs Mail-based orders: What’s the difference?

This is the part most users will misunderstand, so let me explain it clearly.

Requirements before you start

  • Before turning this on, make sure these basics are covered.
  • Your iPhone needs to be running iOS 26 to use Mail-based order tracking.
  • The shopping emails need to be available in Apple’s Mail app. I only used Gmail, so Wallet couldn’t access the order emails. It was fixed after I added that email account to Mail.
  • You must enable Apple Intelligence on your supported iPhone, like an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 16, iPhone 17, or iPhone Air.
  • The feature is available for English (US, UK).

How to turn on order tracking in iOS 26 Wallet

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap Wallet & Apple Pay.
  3. Scroll down and tap Order Tracking.
  4. Turn on Mail.

In my testing, the Wallet app took a while to populate the details from Mail. It worked smoothly after receiving a fresh order confirmation or shipping email. Also, nearly all my purchases from Amazon and Best Buy were listed on Wallet.

You can also try tracking from inside Mail:

  1. Open the Mail app.
  2. Open an order-related email.
  3. Tap Track if the button appears.
  4. Tap Allow when prompted.

How to find your order details in the Wallet app

Once the feature is enabled, here is where to look:

  1. Open the Wallet app.
  2. Tap the More button.
  3. Tap Orders.
  4. Select an order to view its details, like order status, estimated arrival date, shipping progress, and tracking number.
  5. Tap Manage Order to visit the shopping website and make changes.
  6. To contact the seller, select Email This Merchant.
  7. You can also view the payment details from Order Total.

The Wallet app also lists the related emails in one thread so you can stay updated. Scroll to the Related Emails section and select an email to view its details. However, if you are bombarded with tracking alerts, you can disable them from the three-dot icon > Mute Notifications.

When I need to share the purchase information with others, I simply tap the share button in the order details instead of finding and forwarding the email. I know Wallet is still not perfect for deleting my courier apps yet, but it feels like a practical package shipment dashboard.

Tip: If you find a credit/debit card transaction in the Wallet app that you can’t remember, tap it to directly see its Order Tracking details.

Why are my orders not showing up in the iPhone Wallet app

If your orders are not showing in Wallet, do not assume the feature is broken immediately. It is more likely one of these things is happening.

My stance: if Wallet misses one order, that does not make the feature useless. But if it misses most of your orders, it is not ready to replace a dedicated package tracker for you.

The Wallet app finally feels useful for online orders!

iOS 26 turns Wallet order tracking from a nice Apple Pay extra into something normal people might actually use.

The feature still has limits and doesn’t solve messy e-commerce tracking. But the direction is right. Instead of forcing me to remember where I bought something, which courier has it, and which email contains the tracking link, Wallet can now act like a central order board.

My final take is turn it on, but do not trust it blindly yet. Use Wallet for quick order checks. Use the merchant or courier app when you need returns, delivery instructions, proof of delivery, or detailed shipment history.

What do you think about this underrated Wallet feature? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

Read more:

  • How to track your Apple product shipments
  • Apple Wallet vs Google Wallet
  • How to remotely disable Apple Pay when an iPhone is lost or stolen
  • iOS 27 Apple Wallet New Features

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to use Gemini for WhatsApp messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says Gemini interactions depend on the permissions and connected app settings you allow. You can disable WhatsApp integration anytime inside Gemini settings. Personally, I would avoid using it when discussing banking matters or any personal stuff, such as passwords and work details.

mainEntity.name: Can Gemini reply automatically?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. Gemini assists you in composing replies and sending them using voice commands. But it does not autonomously run your WhatsApp conversations. You’re still the one approving and sending messages.

mainEntity.name: Which Roblox account details are sensitive information?

acceptedAnswer.text: Details such as your password and two-step verification code are sensitive information and should never be shared with others.

mainEntity.name: What happens if my Roblox account gets hacked?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your Roblox account falls victim to a hack, firstly, you may lose all access to it. That means losing your in-game progress in Roblox experiences, your Robux balance, your inventory items such as Limiteds, and even saved payment details. Importantly, you should inform Roblox's support team in the event that you lose account access.

mainEntity.name: Can I share my email linked to Roblox with others?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it is generally safe to share your email linked to Roblox with others. However, you should never share other critical Roblox account details, like your password, with anyone else.

title.rendered: Android XR explained: Everything you need to know about Google’s XR platform

content.rendered:
XR headsets have struggled to move beyond niche tech products. Many devices looked futuristic during demos, but high prices, bulky designs, and limited real-world usefulness kept them from becoming mainstream.

Now, Google is trying again with Android XR, a new platform designed for smart glasses, mixed reality headsets, and AI-powered wearable devices. This time, the company believes Gemini AI could finally make XR products practical instead of experimental.

Here’s everything you need to know about Android XR, how it works, and why it matters.

What is Android XR?

Showcased at Google I/O 2026, Android XR is Google’s new operating system for smart glasses, mixed reality headsets, and other immersive wearable devices. XR stands for “Extended Reality,” a category that includes augmented reality, virtual reality, and mixed reality experiences.

Simply put, Android XR is Google’s attempt to create an Android ecosystem beyond smartphones. The platform is meant to power everything from immersive headsets to lightweight smart glasses while keeping Android apps and Google services at the center of the experience.

Instead of building separate software for every device category, Android XR is designed to become a unified foundation for future wearable computing products.

Why Google is betting big on XR again

Google has explored wearable technology before. Products like Google Glass created enormous hype but never truly became mainstream, while earlier VR efforts struggled to attract long-term consumer interest.

The company now believes AI changes the equation completely. Previous smart glasses mostly acted like secondary phone screens. Android XR is being built around Gemini Intelligence, allowing devices to understand voice, surroundings, visual information, and context in real time. That changes how interaction works because users rely less on traditional app navigation.

Google seems to view XR as the next major computing shift after smartphones, and AI is what could finally make that transition believable.

Android XR could make smart glasses actually useful

One of the biggest problems with older smart glasses was that they rarely solved real problems better than a phone. Android XR could change that.

Google demonstrated concepts where lightweight glasses can:

  • Translate conversations live
  • Show navigation directions in front of your eyes
  • Identify landmarks and objects
  • Answer contextual questions
  • Display notifications naturally
  • Provide AI-powered assistance throughout the day

Instead of feeling like mini smartphones on your face, Android XR devices are supposed to work more like intelligent assistants that blend into daily life.

This makes more sense for wearable devices because information appears only when it is relevant to the situation around the user. It feels less like using another screen and more like getting help exactly when needed.

How Gemini AI changes the XR experience

Google is building Android XR around Gemini AI with the idea that users should not have to constantly jump between apps, menus, and voice commands while using smart glasses or headsets.

The platform is designed to let Gemini Omni process visual information, conversations, screens, and surroundings continuously through cameras and sensors built into XR devices. That allows the system to respond based on what the user is actively looking at or doing in the moment.

For example, Gemini could:

  • Summarize documents you’re viewing
  • Explain the objects around you
  • Translate signs instantly
  • Help during presentations or meetings
  • Assist while traveling
  • Organize information visually in virtual spaces

Google clearly wants AI to become the main interface instead of apps and menus. That creates a noticeably different experience compared to traditional voice assistants, which mainly respond to isolated prompts and commands.

With Android XR, Google wants Gemini to function more like a persistent layer operating across the entire interface rather than an assistant users interact with occasionally.

Android XR vs Apple visionOS

When will Android XR launch?

Android XR is expected to arrive later this year alongside the first wave of compatible hardware.

Samsung is reportedly preparing to launch its Android XR-powered smart glasses in July, which could become the first major consumer device running the platform. Meanwhile, Google is also expected to introduce its own smart glasses sometime this fall.

Google has already previewed Android XR publicly and demonstrated several Gemini-powered experiences, but the company is still in the early stages of turning those concepts into commercial products.

The upcoming launches from Samsung and Google will likely determine how ready Android XR truly is for mainstream users. They should also give us a clearer picture of Google’s long-term strategy for AI-powered wearables and spatial computing devices.

Google’s XR vision…

Android XR represents a much bigger shift for Google than simply launching another VR or smart glasses platform. It is Google’s attempt to build an AI-first operating system for the next wave of wearable and spatial devices.

The platform still has plenty to prove once actual products arrive later this year. Until people start using Android XR devices outside controlled demos, it will remain difficult to judge how useful the experience truly feels in everyday situations.

Even so, Android XR offers the clearest look yet at how Google sees AI-powered computing evolving beyond smartphones.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to use Gemini for WhatsApp messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says Gemini interactions depend on the permissions and connected app settings you allow. You can disable WhatsApp integration anytime inside Gemini settings. Personally, I would avoid using it when discussing banking matters or any personal stuff, such as passwords and work details.

mainEntity.name: Can Gemini reply automatically?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. Gemini assists you in composing replies and sending them using voice commands. But it does not autonomously run your WhatsApp conversations. You’re still the one approving and sending messages.

mainEntity.name: Which Roblox account details are sensitive information?

acceptedAnswer.text: Details such as your password and two-step verification code are sensitive information and should never be shared with others.

mainEntity.name: What happens if my Roblox account gets hacked?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your Roblox account falls victim to a hack, firstly, you may lose all access to it. That means losing your in-game progress in Roblox experiences, your Robux balance, your inventory items such as Limiteds, and even saved payment details. Importantly, you should inform Roblox's support team in the event that you lose account access.

mainEntity.name: Can I share my email linked to Roblox with others?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it is generally safe to share your email linked to Roblox with others. However, you should never share other critical Roblox account details, like your password, with anyone else.

Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: These Gemini tricks help me finish long YouTube videos much faster

content.rendered:
I used to open long YouTube videos with good intentions, then quit halfway because I didn’t have 40 minutes to spare. Later, those same videos would sit in my Watch Later list forever. If you are struggling with the same problem, you are in the right place.

Recently, I found a much faster way to pull out the key points from a video without watching every second. The trick is not simply to “watch faster.” It is to use Gemini to decide which sections are actually worth your time. It feels like having a smart shortcut for long tutorials, podcasts, interviews, reviews, and explainers.

Here’s how I use Gemini to finish long YouTube videos faster without missing the parts that actually matter.

Why I don’t just watch videos at 2x speed anymore

Watching videos at 2x speed used to feel productive. But after a while, I realized I was often just wasting time faster.

The problem with 2x speed is that you are still watching the whole video. Most long YouTube videos are not built efficiently. They usually include a slow intro, repeated points, a sponsor section, background context you may already know, and a conclusion that mostly restates the title.

So now, before I watch a long video, I ask Gemini whether I should watch it at all. That one step makes a huge difference. At 2x speed, a 40-minute video still takes 20 minutes. With Gemini, I can usually understand whether I need to watch the full video, only one section, or nothing beyond the summary.

This approach is especially useful for tutorials, product reviews, AI tool demos, interviews, and long explainers where the title sounds useful but the actual value may be buried somewhere in the middle.

First, enable the YouTube extension in Gemini

To use the following tricks properly, you need to turn on the YouTube extension in Gemini. This helps Gemini recognize pasted YouTube URLs correctly and use YouTube context more effectively when generating a response.

Here’s how to enable it:

  1. Open Gemini in a browser, click Settings, then go to Extensions. If you can’t find it, go directly to Gemini apps.
  2. From there, find YouTube and toggle it on.
  3. If Gemini asks for permission, click Connect so extensions can work properly.

Once that is done, you are ready to use Gemini as a smarter way to watch YouTube tutorials, reviews, podcasts, and playlists.

Method 1: I ask Gemini if the video is worth my time

This is the first thing I do now. Before I watch a long video, I ask Gemini to judge it instead of simply summarizing it. That distinction matters. A summary tells you what the video says. A judgment tells you whether you should care.

Here’s the prompt I use:

“Tell me if this YouTube video is worth my time.

Explain:

  • Who this video is useful for.
  • Who can skip it?
  • What problem does it actually solve?
  • Whether the title matches the content.
  • Whether I should watch the full video or only selected parts.”

This works especially well for videos with ambitious titles like “Everything You Need to Know About” or “The Only Guide You’ll Ever Need.” When I tested this with long tech tutorials, Gemini helped me understand whether the video was beginner-friendly, practical, too basic, or filled with unnecessary context.

The most useful part is asking who can skip it. That forces Gemini to be more critical. If you only ask, “What is this video about?” you will usually get a polite summary. But when you ask, “Who should skip this?” the answer becomes much more useful.

My favorite version of this prompt is even sharper: “Be strict. If this video is mostly filler, tell me. If only one section is useful, tell me which one.”

That prompt is great when you are trying to clean up your Watch Later list and do not want to spend time on videos that only sound useful.

Method 2: Gemini helps turn the video into notes and a step-by-step checklist

This is where Gemini becomes more than a YouTube summary tool. I use this method mostly for long tutorials, app walkthroughs, coding videos, AI tool demos, and productivity videos. Instead of replaying the same section again and again, I ask Gemini to extract the steps for me.

Here’s the prompt:

“Turn this YouTube video into clean notes and a step-by-step checklist and export it to a Google Keep note for me to follow.

Include:

  • The main idea
  • Important details
  • Every action I need to take, tools or apps mentioned
  • Settings I need to change
  • Commands or steps shown
  • Mistakes to avoid
  • The final result I should expect.”

Gemini analyzes the video, including its chapters and transcript when available, and pulls out the process in a cleaner format. With setup-style videos, the checklist format is far easier to follow and share with others. I can keep the checklist open, follow each step, and return to the video only when I need to see a visual detail.

For learning videos, I use a slightly different prompt: Turn this video into study notes. Include: key concepts, definitions, examples, important warnings, practical takeaways, and a short recap at the end.

And if I want to actually remember the topic, I add: Create a short quiz from these notes with answers. This turns a long video into something closer to a mini-lesson.

Method 3: Enable the Gemini sidebar for quick information

The Gemini sidebar is the method I use when I do not want to break my flow. Instead of copying things back and forth, I can keep the video open and ask Gemini for quick help while I am watching. The feature is useful enough that even Samsung browser on Windows offers a similar side panel experience.

To use it, click the Ask Gemini button at the right corner of the browser window. Once the sidebar opens, you can ask quick questions like:

  • What is the main point of this video so far?
  • Give me the timestamp for when each feature one is first discussed in the video.
  • What should I pay attention to in this section?
  • Which video should I watch first in this playlist to understand the core feature?

The sidebar is also useful when a video mentions a concept you only half-understand. Instead of pausing the video, opening a new tab, searching Google, and reading three articles, you can ask Gemini directly.

If you use the same prompts often, Gemini’s Skills feature can also help you reuse them faster. You can create a repeatable workflow for summaries, notes, checklists, reviews, or learning prompts.

You can also click the Ask button under the video playback to chat with Gemini.

Bonus: Use NotebookLM to turn a playlist into a knowledge hub

Gemini is great for one video. But if I am dealing with a full playlist, I prefer NotebookLM.

Chrome offers a YouTube to NotebookLM extension that lets you import videos from a YouTube playlist into a notebook. In a few minutes, you can get transcripts from those videos and turn the entire playlist into something much easier to study.

Once you have added all sources, open NotebookLM and use the Audio Overview feature to generate a podcast-style explanation from the videos. I use this to condense the main ideas and customize the format based on what I need.

If podcasts are not your style, you can turn the playlist into notes, FAQs, study questions, summaries, and topic-based breakdowns.

For example, you can use a follow-up prompt like: What are the advanced concepts that connect videos 2, 3, and 5?

NotebookLM can answer like a tutor and give automatic suggestions. You can click Save to note and then Convert to source to keep those insights inside the notebook.

This works especially well for learning technical topics. If I am watching a playlist about an AI tool, a programming concept, a productivity system, or a software workflow, I do not want ten disconnected summaries. I want one organized learning hub that helps me understand how everything connects.

My favorite Gemini prompts for long YouTube videos

These are the prompts I keep coming back to. They work because they don’t ask Gemini to be vague. They force it to make decisions.

1. The Be Strict prompt

Be strict. If this video is too long for the value it provides, tell me.

Include:
- what is useful
- what is filler
- what is repeated
- what I should watch
- what I can safely skip

2. The 10-minute version

If I only have 10 minutes, which parts of this video should I watch?

Give me:
- the must-watch sections
- the skippable sections
- the fastest way to understand the video

3. The notes prompt

Turn this video into structured notes.

Use:
- headings
- bullet points
- examples
- definitions
- practical takeaways

4. The review prompt

Summarize this review into:
- pros
- cons
- deal-breakers
- who should buy it
- who should avoid it
- final verdict

5. The Podcast prompt

Group the best ideas from this conversation by topic.

Tell me:
- the strongest points
- the most interesting arguments
- the parts worth watching
- the parts that are repetitive

6. The learning prompt

Teach me the topic from this video like I am new to it.

Then give me:
- simple notes
- examples
- common mistakes
- a short quiz with answers

That last one is my favorite when I’m cleaning up my Watch Later list. It turns a video into study material.

What I still watch manually

Gemini can’t replace watching videos completely. There are still some instances wherein I have to view the video manually, such as software demos, UI walkthroughs, coding steps, product footage, camera samples, design work, and anything where the creator is showing something instead of just explaining it.

I also watch manually when the topic is high-stakes or easy to misunderstand. These topics include videos related to health, money, law, security, or fast-changing news.

Additionally, AI summaries can miss nuance. They may flatten opinions or make uncertain points sound cleaner than they really are. And sometimes the most valuable part of a video can be a small demo, a warning, or an offhand comment. That’s why I still decide what to trust.

Watch YouTube smartly with Gemini!

Long YouTube videos are still useful, but I no longer treat them like something I have to watch from start to finish. With Gemini, I can quickly understand the main points, find the sections that matter, and skip the parts that do not add much value.

For me, these tricks make YouTube feel less overwhelming. Whether I am watching a tutorial, interview, podcast, or explainer, Gemini helps me save time while still getting the information I came for.

What do you think about these Gemini features? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to use Gemini for WhatsApp messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says Gemini interactions depend on the permissions and connected app settings you allow. You can disable WhatsApp integration anytime inside Gemini settings. Personally, I would avoid using it when discussing banking matters or any personal stuff, such as passwords and work details.

mainEntity.name: Can Gemini reply automatically?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. Gemini assists you in composing replies and sending them using voice commands. But it does not autonomously run your WhatsApp conversations. You’re still the one approving and sending messages.

title.rendered: Perplexity’s AI browser for iPhone just got a big upgrade

content.rendered:
Perplexity has released a major update for its Comet app on iPhone and iPad, adding several new usability improvements and interface upgrades.

Comet combines traditional web browsing with AI-powered assistance, allowing users to search the web, interact with AI chatbots, and use webpage context during conversations.

The AI-powered browser first launched on Mac before expanding to iPhone and iPad earlier this year.

Comet for iPhone and iPad now includes eight major upgrades

According to Perplexity, the latest update introduces eight major improvements across the app experience.

The new additions include:

  1. One-tap phone number actions for calling, FaceTime, messaging, or saving contacts directly from webpages.
  2. A redesigned iPad sidebar with smoother animations and a cleaner layout.
  3. Finance Deep Dive analysis now opens inside dedicated browser tabs.
  4. Search results now remember their previous position when users switch between pages.
  5. Support for dragging images directly into the AI assistant.
  6. An adaptive omni-box that changes more smoothly between light and dark websites.
  7. Fixed behavior for clearing Recently Closed tabs.
  8. Deleted chat threads now stay permanently deleted.

The company also says the update includes multiple bug fixes and visual refinements.

The update also improves stability and iPhone navigation

Alongside the headline features, Perplexity says it has fixed crashes tied to clearing browsing data and closing tabs.

The company also mentions:

  • Sharper and more stable favicons
  • Cleaner bottom controls on iPhone
  • General interface polish and stability improvements

Perplexity has been steadily expanding Comet’s feature set since bringing the browser from Mac to iOS earlier this year.

The updates show the company continuing to position Comet as more than just a chatbot app by turning it into a full AI-focused browsing experience across Apple devices.

Would you use an AI browser like Comet instead of Safari or Chrome? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to use Gemini for WhatsApp messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says Gemini interactions depend on the permissions and connected app settings you allow. You can disable WhatsApp integration anytime inside Gemini settings. Personally, I would avoid using it when discussing banking matters or any personal stuff, such as passwords and work details.

mainEntity.name: Can Gemini reply automatically?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. Gemini assists you in composing replies and sending them using voice commands. But it does not autonomously run your WhatsApp conversations. You’re still the one approving and sending messages.

acceptedAnswer.text: Details such as your password and two-step verification code are sensitive information and should never be shared with others.

mainEntity.name: What happens if my Roblox account gets hacked?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your Roblox account falls victim to a hack, firstly, you may lose all access to it. Importantly, you should inform Roblox's support team in the event that you lose account access.

title.rendered: Spotify is expanding into AI music creation with new remix features

content.rendered:
Spotify has announced a range of new features focused on AI-generated music tools, fan-made remixes, and concert ticket reservations as part of its Investor Day 2026 announcements.

The company says upcoming updates will include AI-powered remix and cover creation tools for music fans, alongside a new concert ticket feature called Reserved for Premium subscribers.

Spotify is bringing AI-generated remixes and fan-made covers

Spotify has signed new licensing agreements with Universal Music Group that will allow fans to create AI-generated covers and remixes using licensed music.

The feature will let fans create remixes and alternate versions of songs from participating artists and songwriters directly inside Spotify.

The company says the system is designed to create a way for artists and rights holders to earn from AI-generated remixes tied to their music. Spotify plans to offer the AI remix and fan-made cover tools as a paid add-on for Premium subscribers.

This expands Spotify’s AI strategy beyond recommendations and discovery into actual music creation.

Spotify also wants to make concert ticket buying easier

Spotify also introduced a new feature called Reserved, which will temporarily hold concert tickets for eligible Premium users in the United States.

Reserved is aimed at dedicated fans rather than casual ticket buyers or scalpers. Eligibility will reportedly depend on listening history and artist engagement inside Spotify.

According to Spotify, some users may be able to reserve up to two tickets before they become publicly available.

Introducing Reserved. Concert tickets held just for you based on your listening 🎫 Stay tuned – Reserved tickets are coming to Premium users in the US. pic.twitter.com/BqGttMJHFI

— Spotify (@Spotify) May 21, 2026

The company hasn’t shared complete details about how Reserved will work in practice, though Spotify says more information will be available closer to launch.

Spotify also announced additional podcast and audiobook updates during Investor Day 2026, though the company has not fully detailed those features yet.

Together, the updates show Spotify moving beyond passive music streaming toward a platform where listening, creation, and live events are becoming more connected.

Would you use Spotify’s AI remix tools to create your own song versions? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

acceptedAnswer.text: If your Roblox account falls victim to a hack, firstly, you may lose all access to it. title.rendered: OpenAI adds Appshots to Codex for Mac so you can show context instantly

content.rendered:
OpenAI has updated Codex for Mac with a new feature called Appshots, giving users a faster way to show the coding agent what they are looking at in another Mac app.

According to OpenAI’s Codex changelog, Appshots are available in Codex app version 26.519 on macOS. Pressing both Command keys sends the frontmost app window to a Codex thread with a screenshot and available text, so the user does not have to manually describe the page, error, email, design, or settings screen.

Appshots make Mac app context easier to share

The idea is simple: instead of copying text into Codex or writing a long setup prompt, you can show Codex the current window and ask for help.

OpenAI’s Appshots documentation says the feature captures only the frontmost window. It can include an image of the visible window and text the app makes available, including some text beyond the visible scroll area when the app exposes it.

That could be useful for tasks where visual or app state matters. OpenAI gives examples such as sharing an API reference page, an email or calendar view, an image editor, a design preview, an error message, or a settings panel. For developers, the most obvious use case is giving Codex a live view of a bug, UI state, or documentation page before asking it to change code.

It’s Codex Thursday, and yes, we have updates for you.

First up: Appshots, a new way to bring the context of what you’re working on into Codex.

On your Mac, press Command-Command to attach your app window to a Codex thread. Codex gets both a screenshot and text from the window,… pic.twitter.com/R0EcZRCc1d

— OpenAI Developers (@OpenAIDevs) May 21, 2026

By default, Codex starts a new thread for an appshot. If the user recently interacted with a Codex thread, OpenAI says the appshot is added to that thread instead. Consecutive appshots also go into the same thread.

There are permission and privacy limits

Appshots are not a silent background capture feature. The user has to trigger them from the Codex app on macOS using both Command keys or a custom hotkey.

Codex may also ask for macOS permissions before the feature works. Screen & System Audio Recording lets it capture the window image, while Accessibility lets it read available text from the frontmost window.

OpenAI says appshots are stored locally in the session file, like files or images attached manually. Still, the captured image and available text are shared with Codex when the user takes an appshot, so sensitive windows should stay out of the flow unless the task really needs them.

There are also app-specific limits. For some apps and websites, including Google Docs, Gmail, Google Sheets, and Google Slides, Codex may receive only the visible screenshot and not the full document or off-screen text. Existing appshots can remain in a thread when resumed in the CLI, but new appshots can only be created from the Codex app on macOS.

Codex also gets goal mode and locked remote use

Appshots headline the update, but OpenAI bundled several other Codex changes into the same release.

Goal mode is now generally available in the Codex app, IDE extension, and CLI. It lets users give Codex a specific objective and success criteria, then keep the agent working toward that goal across longer tasks. OpenAI positions it for work that may stretch across hours or days, with the user able to check in, steer, pause, or resume.

The update also adds locked computer use for eligible Mac users. OpenAI’s Computer Use docs say Codex can keep using desktop apps after the Mac locks, including from a connected device, but only after the user enables the setting. The feature is scoped to active, trusted Computer Use turns and includes safeguards such as covered displays and relocking when local input is detected.

That builds on last week’s Codex remote access in the ChatGPT mobile app, where users gained the ability to follow and steer Codex work from iPhone, iPad, and Android while the actual work continued on a connected Mac host.

OpenAI is making Codex more context-aware

The broader direction is clear: OpenAI wants Codex to spend less time waiting for perfect prompts and more time working with the context already on the user’s machine.

Appshots help with the first step by making it easier to hand over a window. Goal mode helps Codex stay aimed at a longer outcome. Locked computer use and mobile access make it easier to keep a task moving when the user is away from the Mac.

For Mac users, Appshots may be the most immediately useful change. It turns “look at this” into a hotkey, which is exactly the kind of small workflow shortcut that can make an AI coding agent feel less like a separate tool and more like part of the desktop.

excerpt.rendered: OpenAI’s latest Codex for Mac update adds Appshots, a hotkey-powered way to send an app window, screenshot, and available text to a Codex thread.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to use Gemini for WhatsApp messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says Gemini interactions depend on the permissions and connected app settings you allow. You can disable WhatsApp integration anytime inside Gemini settings. Personally, I would avoid using it when discussing banking matters or any personal stuff, such as passwords and work details.

mainEntity.name: Can Gemini reply automatically?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. Gemini assists you in composing replies and sending them using voice commands. But it does not autonomously run your WhatsApp conversations. You’re still the one approving and sending messages.

title.rendered: Gemini Omni explained: What it is, how it works, and why it’s Google’s biggest AI upgrade yet

content.rendered:
At Google I/O 2026, Google introduced Gemini Omni, a new AI model built to understand text, images, video, audio, and live interactions together. The company describes it as a major step toward creating a more fluid AI experience across devices, where AI can understand context across multiple formats simultaneously.

Instead of treating text, visuals, and voice as separate inputs, Gemini Omni processes everything within a unified system. Users can move between voice conversations, visuals, typed prompts, and live camera input without interrupting the interaction.

Here’s everything you need to know about Gemini Omni and why Google considers it one of its most important AI launches yet.

What is Gemini Omni?

Gemini Omni is a multimodal AI model that can process different types of information simultaneously. Users can speak naturally, upload visuals, share live camera input, and continue conversations without switching between separate tools.

During Google’s demos, Gemini Omni could analyze surroundings in real time and respond contextually while the interaction continued naturally. For example, someone could point their phone camera at a landmark, ask a spoken question, and receive instant answers without manually typing anything.

Google plans to integrate Gemini Omni across Android, Search, Chrome, YouTube, Gmail, Workspace apps, and upcoming Android XR devices.

How Gemini Omni differs from ChatGPT and Copilot

OpenAI ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot already offer image understanding, voice support, and AI assistance for different tasks. Gemini Omni enters the same space, though Google is integrating it far more deeply across its own ecosystem.

At I/O 2026, Google showed Gemini Omni working inside Search, Android, and Android XR glasses while handling voice conversations and live camera input in real time.

ChatGPT is still widely used for writing, brainstorming, and general conversations. Microsoft Copilot is more closely linked with Microsoft apps like Word and Excel. Gemini Omni appears focused on helping users interact with Google services more naturally across phones, Search, and wearable devices.

Why Google is focusing on multimodal AI

Google is pushing multimodal AI because people do much more than type while using their devices. They speak, use cameras, share screenshots, watch videos, and interact with apps continuously throughout the day.

Gemini Omni is designed around those everyday interactions. Instead of relying only on text prompts, the model can respond using visual input, voice conversations, and live surroundings at the same time. Google plans to use this technology across Search, Android devices, and upcoming XR products.

This direction also helps Google expand AI beyond smartphones into products like Android XR glasses and future wearable devices.

Gemini Omni also connects closely with Gemini Intelligence, the company’s broader effort to bring AI-powered features deeper into Android and future wearable devices.

Real-world ways Gemini Omni could be used

Gemini Omni introduces several practical use cases that go beyond chatbot conversations.

Possible applications include:

  • Live language translation through Gemini AI-powered glasses
  • Visual assistance while traveling
  • Instant answers about nearby objects or landmarks
  • AI-assisted shopping inside Google Search
  • Automatic email and notification summaries
  • Hands-free navigation support
  • Interactive learning experiences for students
  • Context-aware recommendations during daily tasks

The company also demonstrated Gemini Omni handling ongoing voice conversations while understanding live surroundings in real time, creating interactions that felt closer to speaking with an assistant that can actually “see” what the user is seeing.

Gemini Omni could reshape Google Search

One of the biggest goals behind Gemini Omni is transforming Google Search from a list of links into a more interactive experience.

Instead of typing short keywords and opening multiple websites manually, users can now ask detailed questions, continue conversations naturally, and even search using voice, images, or live camera input.

During I/O 2026, Google showed Search generating detailed responses directly inside results pages while continuing conversations without forcing users to restart queries repeatedly.

Gemini Omni also helps Search understand context more accurately, making Search more responsive during complex or visually driven queries.

Google’s larger goal appears focused on making Search feel less like a traditional search engine and more like an intelligent assistant woven directly into everyday browsing.

Concerns around Gemini Omni

No matter how useful Google portrays Gemini Omni, its launch also raises questions around:

  • Privacy
  • AI accuracy
  • Data collection
  • Website traffic reduction
  • Ownership of AI-generated content

Since Gemini Omni relies heavily on contextual understanding and live interactions, users may share larger amounts of personal information with AI systems during regular usage.

Publishers and creators are also watching Google’s AI Search direction closely as AI-generated responses become more prominent inside search results.

Google’s biggest AI bet yet…

Gemini Omni represents a major shift in how Google wants people to interact with technology. Rather than functioning as a standalone chatbot, Gemini Omni is becoming deeply integrated into Google’s broader ecosystem. The model now sits across Search, Android, wearable devices, and several core Google services, making it one of the company’s biggest long-term technology projects in years.

Do you think Gemini Omni can actually change how people use Search and smart devices daily? Let us know in the comments.

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says Gemini interactions depend on the permissions and connected app settings you allow. You can disable WhatsApp integration anytime inside Gemini settings. Personally, I would avoid using it when discussing banking matters or any personal stuff, such as passwords and work details.

mainEntity.name: Can Gemini reply automatically?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. Gemini assists you in composing replies and sending them using voice commands. But it does not autonomously run your WhatsApp conversations. You’re still the one approving and sending messages.

That means losing your in-game progress in Roblox experiences, your Robux balance, your inventory items such as Limiteds, and even saved payment details. Importantly, you should inform Roblox's support team in the event that you lose account access.

mainEntity.name: Can I share my email linked to Roblox with others?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it is generally safe to share your email linked to Roblox with others. However, you should never share other critical Roblox account details, like your password, with anyone else.

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: Samsung Browser is now on Windows: 6 reasons I switched from Google Chrome

content.rendered:
Samsung has officially launched Samsung Browser for Windows, bringing its mobile browsing experience to PCs with cross-device continuity, Samsung Pass integration, and new built-in agentic AI features. You may access the browser on Windows 11 and Windows 10 1809 or later versions.

I installed the Samsung Browser mainly to test the new features on Windows. But after using it with my Galaxy phone and Samsung account, I realized it can be a good alternative to Chrome. Here is my hands-on comparison of Samsung Browser vs Google Chrome — what felt better, what still needs work, and who should actually switch.

What is Samsung Browser for Windows?

Samsung Browser for Windows is the desktop version of Samsung’s mobile browser, previously known as Samsung Internet.

Samsung says the browser can sync bookmarks and browsing history via Samsung Cloud, let users pick up where they left off between mobile and PC, and integrate with Samsung Pass for secure website sign-ins and autofill. That makes it different from other Chromium-style browsers.

The new browser includes an AI assistant with Perplexity technology that understands human language and can analyze the page and activities on other tabs. Hence, it allows the user to explore content, manage tabs, navigate browsing history, and stay productive without leaving the browser.

6 reasons I switched to Samsung Browser from Chrome

To enjoy all these features, you need to download Samsung Browser on your Windows PC or laptop and log in using the same Samsung account you have on your Galaxy device.

Surprisingly, some features even work on other Android phones. Simply install Samsung Internet on your Android and create a Samsung Cloud account if you don’t have one. Then log in to your Windows machine.

1. My Galaxy phone finally felt connected to my Windows PC

My first motivation to switch was very simple; Samsung Browser allowed me to make my Galaxy phone and Windows computer work in one flow.

Chrome already syncs well across devices, but it syncs around your Google account. Samsung Browser syncs with your Samsung Cloud. That difference matters if you already use Samsung Internet on Android. Along with basic bookmark and history sync, Samsung lets users pick up where they left off when moving between mobile and PC.

I am constantly jumping between devices. I read something on my phone, leave it halfway, open my laptop, search again, and waste time rebuilding the same browsing session. Samsung Browser shows a continuity icon at the top right corner. Clicking it opens up my phone’s tab directly. It even jumps right to my exact scrolling position.

For someone who reads articles, checks product pages, researches topics, and saves links throughout the day, the continuity saves lots of time and effort.

2. Samsung Pass made sign-ins feel less annoying

I did not realize how much browser switching depends on passwords until I tried moving away from Chrome. All of my passwords and autofill data, like credit card details and saved addresses, were saved on my Galaxy’s Samsung account and PC’s Chrome password manager.

Samsung Browser avoids that problem by leaning on Samsung Pass. The integration lets users securely store personal information, sign in to websites, and autofill profiles across devices and apps.

When you are installing the browser, it prompts you to enable Samsung Pass. If you have skipped it, then worry not. Follow the steps below:

  1. Click on your profile picture on the menu bar of the browser.
  2. Select Sync settings from the dropdown.
  3. Here, toggle on Samsung Pass.

Instead of treating my PC browser and phone password flow like two separate worlds, Samsung Browser made sign-ins feel closer to what I already use on my Galaxy phone. It felt less like switching browsers and more like extending my existing setup.

Would I tell a Google Password Manager user to switch only for this? No. But if your sign-ins already live in Samsung’s ecosystem, Samsung Browser becomes much easier to adopt.

3. Privacy features feel more visible than Chrome’s

I would not claim Samsung Browser is automatically more private than Chrome for every user. But Samsung makes privacy feel more visible.

Chrome has strong security features, but it also carries the baggage of being Google’s browser. You will come across lots of pop-ups, ads, and trackers while browsing. And the recent update has stopped many ad-blocker extensions

Samsung Browser offers smart anti-tracking, ad and pop-up blocking, and backward redirection prevention. It prompts you to enable an ad blocker while setting up. I also liked its Privacy Dashboard, which shows the total number of trackers and ads blocked in the last 24 hours. Simply, click the hamburger menu and go to Ad blocker > Privacy settings.

The built-in ad blocker also helps the web page to load faster and doesn’t weigh down the CPU like extensions. Moreover, you can access Secret Mode to go incognito. But you can lock those tabs similar to Safari’s Private Browsing. All these features made me trust the browser more.

4. The sidebar and layout made daily browsing and multi-tasking faster

The sidebar is the feature that made Samsung Browser feel different from Chrome for me, especially when working with a single screen.

Instead of only using it as a tab-heavy browser, I could pin frequently used sites like Google, YouTube, Amazon, and many more to the sidebar and open them in a narrow side panel beside my main page. It’s like a secondary browser. For daily browsing and research, this layout made Samsung Internet feel faster, cleaner, and better suited for multitasking.

You can even access your open tabs and Quick access shortcuts across your synced devices. Moreover, I can track events and tasks through the calendar shortcut. Therefore, if you constantly lose track of your tabs, it’s a lifesaver.

In terms of interface, Samsung Browser is cleaner than Chrome. The menu and URL bar are movable, and you can even pin the address bar to the bottom. Moreover, it lets me choose different tab layouts like Stack, List, and Grid to accommodate all the pages opened at once.

5. The Agentic AI features make more sense inside a browser

After seeing what Gemini in Chrome is trying to do, Samsung’s browser AI direction feels easier to understand. Google is turning Chrome into an AI layer that can summarize pages, answer questions from open tabs, compare information, and even move toward “auto browse” tasks.

Samsung’s pitch feels similar in spirit, but more focused on making its own browser useful across phone and PC, not just adding another chatbot button. In partnership with Perplexity, Samsung is giving users the following features:

  • AI-powered browsing help: Instead of copying a long article into another app, I can ask it to summarize the page, pull out the key points, or explain something in simpler words while I’m still on the site. That feels much more natural than jumping between tabs and AI tools.
  • Smarter search and discovery: No more digging through pages to find the right answer. I simply tell the agentic AI what I am looking for, and it opens the exact web page. This even works for the video content.
  • Task assistance across websites: While comparing products, planning travel, or filling out repetitive forms, you need to go back and forth between the tabs. Now, Samsung AI assistant lets you summarize and compare the content of multiple tabs in one go.
  • Retrieve page from browsing history: Remembering the keyword or date to find a tab in history is quite impossible. So, I prefer asking the Assistant. For example, “Which laptops were I looking at last weekend? Open those webpages.”

Compared with Gemini, Samsung’s AI features are still limited. However, they make more sense when tied to Galaxy devices, Samsung Pass, and cross-device browsing continuity.

6. More user control over memory management

We all know how much RAM and memory Chrome hogs on a machine. So, it’s quite difficult to use with low RAM laptops as it drags the whole system down. Samsung’s Optimize memory use feature feels like a more practical answer to that problem.

You can control which websites remain active in the background and which tabs can be unloaded to free up memory. That means the browser is not simply keeping every tab alive at all costs. Instead, it can reclaim resources from tabs I’m not using and give more breathing room to the page I’m actually working on.

  1. Go to Settings in the browser.
  2. Scroll down the left sidebar and select Performance and system.
  3. Here, toggle on Optimize memory use and choose an option suitable for your workflow.

Compared with Chrome, this approach feels more transparent. Chrome has improved over the years with memory-saving features, but it still has a reputation for being heavy, especially on older laptops and budget PCs.

Samsung Browser vs Google Chrome: What changed for me?

After switching, I do not see Samsung Browser as a universal Chrome killer. That would be lazy. I see it as a targeted Chrome alternative.

Here is what changed for me:

The biggest change was psychological. Chrome used to feel like the browser I had to use. Samsung Browser made it feel like one option among many. That is a major shift.

Things I wish I knew before switching

Samsung Browser Makes the Most Sense Only If You Use Samsung Devices

  • If you do not use a Galaxy phone, Samsung Browser loses a lot of its magic. The browser is useful on Windows, but the real value comes from the connection between phone and PC.
  • The hardest part was not learning the Samsung Browser. It was breaking the habit of opening Chrome without thinking.
  • Samsung’s agentic AI browser features sound genuinely useful, especially the ability to understand page context and activity across tabs. But they are currently available in the US and South Korea.
  • If your passwords are messy, browser switching becomes painful fast. Make sure that Samsung Pass is compatible with the existing login process. If all your passwords live in Google Password Manager, Chrome still has a strong grip on you.

I switched my daily browsing, but I did not delete Chrome for its extensions, compatibility, testing, and Google-heavy workflows.

Where Chrome is still better

Chrome still wins in the places where maturity matters.

The biggest one is extensions. Chrome’s extension ecosystem is still unmatched. If your workflow depends on specific extensions, Samsung Browser may not replace that setup immediately.

Chrome is also a perfect fit if you live inside Google Workspace, like Gmail, Google Docs, Google Drive, etc. All these feel naturally tied to Chrome.

Developer tools are another advantage. If you are a web developer, Chrome DevTools are still the familiar standard. Though Samsung Browser might be good enough for your daily use, Chrome is definitely more reliable for development and debugging purposes.

Finally, Chrome is more universal. This browser runs seamlessly on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS, Chromebooks, and almost every environment where people browse the web. You can even create different profiles to keep browsing separately.

Who should switch to Samsung Browser?

You should try Samsung Browser on Windows if you use a Galaxy phone and want your PC browsing to feel more connected to your mobile life.

I would especially recommend it if you:

  • Already use Samsung Internet on your phone
  • Use Samsung Pass for passwords and autofill
  • Move between phone and PC throughout the day
  • Want to experience Samsung’s agentic AI features
  • Open Chrome mostly out of habit

Final verdict

I switched from Chrome to Samsung Browser on Windows because Chrome started feeling too generic for my setup.

Though Samsung Browser cannot win over Chrome when it comes to extensions, developer tools, or universal platform support. But it makes my Galaxy phone and Windows PC feel like parts of the same system. That is the reason this browser matters.

Samsung is trying to make the browser part of its larger connected-device and AI strategy and claiming the desktop space it has ignored for too long. o longer feels like the browser built for me.

Will you try the Samsung Browser? Share your opinion in the comments below!

  • How to save AI prompts as Chrome Skills

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to use Gemini for WhatsApp messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says Gemini interactions depend on the permissions and connected app settings you allow. You can disable WhatsApp integration anytime inside Gemini settings. mainEntity.name: Can Gemini reply automatically?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. Gemini assists you in composing replies and sending them using voice commands. But it does not autonomously run your WhatsApp conversations. You’re still the one approving and sending messages.
